hints.content: To translate quadrilateral $ABCD$ using $(x,y)\to(x -5,y )$, we basically translate quadrilateral $ABCD$'s vertices and connect them.

For example, point $\blueD{B(2,-4)}$ is translated to $(2 -5,-4 )=\greenD{(-3,-4)}$.



[[☃ image 1]]

options.alt: A coordinate plane with a quadrilateral having vertices A at one, negative two, B at two, negative four, C at five, two, and D at three, negative one. The x- and y- axes scale by one. A dashed line moves five units left from vertex B to a point at negative three, negative four.

hints.content:
Doing this for all vertices and connecting them, we get the following mapping:



[[☃ image 1]]

options.alt: A coordinate plane with a quadrilateral having vertices A at one, negative two, B at two, negative four, C at five, two, and D at three, negative one. The x- and y- axes scale by one. A dashed line moves five units left from the four vertices to form an image of a congruent quadrilateral with vertices at negative three, negative four, negative four, negative two, negative two, negative one, and zero, two.
